article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Chem 4 × AWOG
Breeder: Rich “One Eye” Crommelin
THC Content: 20–29%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: Myrcene and pinene
Primary Flavors: Diesel, skunk, pine, earth, pepper
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: mid-October
Indoor Yield: 300–400 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 500–600 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Advanced

Dawg Walker OG belongs to a different era of cannabis than today’s dessert-heavy hybrids . Instead of frosting, candy, or tropical fruit dominating the experience, this Pacific Northwest cultivar leads with gasoline, damp earth, pine needles, skunk, and an almost industrial chemical funk. Its smell can be remarkably persistent, lingering in a room long after the flower has been handled. That aggressive aroma is matched by a high that starts surprisingly alert before gradually becoming heavier, calmer, and considerably more physical.

Often written as Dogwalker OG or simply Dog Walker, the original cultivar is associated with Pacific Northwest breeder Rich “One Eye” Crommelin. A CLTVTD Genetics breeder interview specifically credits Crommelin with creating Dog Walker OG, while growers maintaining the One Eye cut describe the pedigree as Chem 4 crossed with AWOG, with AWOG itself representing OG Kush × Albert Walker. Older commercial records sometimes simplify the lineage to Albert Walker OG × Chemdawg 91 , which has contributed to confusion, but the One Eye provenance provides the stronger historical link for the original cut.
Genetics and Lineage

The Chem 4 side supplies much of the cultivar’s unmistakable fuel character. Chem-family marijuana is valued for piercing petroleum, sour chemical, earth, and skunk aromas, along with powerful THC-driven effects. Dawg Walker OG preserves that personality unusually well. Rather than smoothing the Chem influence into sweetness, the cross amplifies its dirty, penetrating character with pine and OG-derived earthiness. Resin production can be substantial, although the plant’s appeal has traditionally centered more on aroma and effect than perfectly manicured modern bag appeal.

AWOG contributes the other half of the equation. Growers preserving the One Eye cut identify AWOG as OG Kush × Albert Walker, adding a mixture of pine, lemon, skunk, earth, and old-school funk to the Chem foundation. Sofresh Farm, which lists its phenotype directly from OneEye, records the lineage as Chem 4 × AWOG and identifies OneEye as both breeder and phenotype source. That background also explains why different lineage descriptions exist: when AWOG is shortened to “Albert Walker,” an important OG Kush component can disappear from the written pedigree.
Effects and Experience

The first portion of the experience can be unexpectedly cerebral. A few inhalations may bring a noticeable shift in attention, a lifted mood, and a calm but focused mental state rather than instant sedation. Music, conversation, and familiar activities can feel more absorbing, while physical tension begins fading gradually in the background. This balance gives moderate amounts more versatility than the heavy OG reputation might imply.

As THC exposure increases, the character changes. Relaxation spreads through the body, movement becomes less appealing, and the earlier mental sharpness can soften into a hazier state. Strong doses may become deeply sedating, particularly late in the day or for consumers without substantial tolerance. Contemporary holders of the original-style cut report potency reaching the upper 20% range, while nursery references place typical examples closer to 20–26%. Dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, and anxiety remain possible THC-related effects, especially with excessive consumption.
Medical Benefits

No clinical research has evaluated Dawg Walker OG itself as a treatment, so its medical reputation should be separated from established evidence about cannabis more broadly. In practice, THC-dominant marijuana with a transition from mental calm to substantial physical relaxation may appeal to patients seeking temporary relief from discomfort, appetite problems, stress, or difficulty settling down at night. Its stronger body effects become more apparent at larger doses, which is one reason the cultivar is often associated with evening use.

Terpenes add aromatic complexity but should not be treated as guaranteed therapeutic predictors. Myrcene and pinene have appeared prominently in preserved-cut descriptions, while broader testing references also identify caryophyllene, humulene, limonene, and linalool. Medical consumers should pay closer attention to the cannabinoid and terpene certificate for the specific batch they are considering rather than expecting every example bearing the strain name to produce identical results.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The aroma is where this weed becomes unmistakable. Fresh flower can smell like diesel fuel spilled across damp forest soil, followed by sharp pine, skunk musk, pepper, and a chemical note that borders on rubber or solvent. Some batches develop a faint citrus quality after grinding, but sweetness remains secondary. Proper curing intensifies the depth, allowing earthy and musky elements to emerge beneath the louder petroleum notes.

Smoke or vapor continues the same theme. Pine and fuel generally arrive first, followed by earthy spice and a lingering Chem-like funk on the exhale. Higher temperatures can emphasize the peppery and skunky qualities, whereas lower-temperature vaporization may reveal more pine, herbs, and subtle citrus. Anyone looking for berry candy or creamy dessert terpenes will find little resemblance here; Dawg Walker OG is fundamentally an old-school gas cultivar.
Growing Information

Cultivation requires more attention than many forgiving commercial hybrids. Nursery data for the One-Eye-associated cut places flowering around 9–10 weeks, with outdoor maturation near mid-October. Indoor production is estimated around 300–400 g/m², although environment and grower skill can move that figure considerably. The plant can become bushy and produce substantial lateral growth, making thoughtful canopy management important for getting light into interior flowering sites.

Selective pruning, branch spreading, and adequate spacing can improve airflow and prevent shaded lower growth from consuming unnecessary resources. Experienced growers have also described the cut as somewhat sensitive, reinforcing the value of gradual nutrient adjustments instead of aggressive feeding. Dense foliage should be managed before late flowering, particularly in humid gardens. Odor control is almost mandatory indoors: the combination of Chem fuel, skunk, and musk can become extraordinarily strong well before harvest.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Dawg Walker OG?

The original One Eye cut is best documented as Chem 4 × AWOG, with AWOG described as OG Kush × Albert Walker. Some sources shorten the lineage to Albert Walker × Chem 4 or list Chemdawg 91 × Albert Walker, which accounts for conflicting descriptions found online.
Who bred Dawg Walker OG?

Pacific Northwest breeder Rich “One Eye” Crommelin is credited with creating the original Dog Walker OG. A breeder-focused CLTVTD Genetics interview identifies Crommelin with Dog Walker OG as well as his later Scooby Snacks hybrid.
Is Dawg Walker OG indica or sativa?
It is generally considered an indica-leaning hybrid. The initial experience can feel focused and cerebral, but stronger physical relaxation typically becomes more prominent as the effects progress.
What does Dawg Walker OG taste like?
Diesel, skunk, pine, earth, pepper, musk, and chemical funk dominate the profile. Some batches reveal light citrus or woody notes beneath the heavier gas characteristics.
How long does Dawg Walker OG take to flower?
Indoor growers should expect approximately nine to ten weeks of flowering. Outdoor plants generally reach maturity around mid-October where autumn weather remains suitable.
Final Thoughts on Dawg Walker OG

Dawg Walker OG has survived changing cannabis trends because it offers something many newer weed strains deliberately breed away from: uncompromising funk. Chem 4, OG Kush, and Albert Walker ancestry converge into an aromatic profile dominated by petroleum, skunk, pine, damp earth, and spice, while the effects move from composed cerebral stimulation toward much deeper physical relaxation.

Its history also makes accurate identification worthwhile. The authentic One Eye cut carries a specific Pacific Northwest legacy, and reducing its pedigree to whichever parent combination appears most frequently online obscures that story. For cannabis enthusiasts interested in classic gas genetics, breeders searching for forceful Chem-and-OG traits, or experienced consumers who prefer pungent weed over sweet dessert profiles, Dawg Walker OG remains a distinctive old-school cultivar with an unusually recognizable character.
